checks: All integer feasible flows and all four cuts were enumerated for both networks.
Initial routing SA=3, SB=3, AT=2, AB=1, BT=4 attains the cut bound of six.
Raising AB capacity to two allows SA=4, SB=3, AT=2, AB=2, BT=5 and a cut bound of seven.
proof: Every source-to-destination unit must cross the cut with S and A on its source side. Its forward capacities bound total flow by 3 + middle + 2. The displayed capacity-respecting conserved routing attains this bound, proving optimality even among real-valued flows.
limits: Moving packets illustrate routes, not measured physical rates. This is a directed capacity model, not a hydraulic-pressure or travel-time model. The film proves the concrete example and names the general theorem.
